snp1.2:1.3: The term _mahī_ (here _mahiyā_) simply means “large, great” (the feminine form of the more common word _mahā_). Although the commentary defines this word as meaning a “religious festival,” there is no support for this in the Canon; however, it is often used as an adjective describing the ocean (MN 82, SN 8.7, KN 8.264, KN 14.310). Given that this context has the term _anutīre_ (“at the shore”), the intended meaning of _mahi_ is therefore likely “a large body of water” rather than “a religious festival.”
snp1.2:2.1: The Buddha is making a pun that is impossible to capture in translation. _Pakkodana_ (cooked rice) and _akkodhana_ (no anger), and _khīra_ (milk) and _khila_ (corruption).
snp1.2:2.4: The imagery of the “extinguished fire” is clearly a reference to awakening (ie, the fires of defilement and delusion have been extinguished). The “open hut” (_vivaṭā kuṭi_) may be referring to the mind being clear and alert, as the word _vivaṭa_ has that meaning elsewhere in the suttas.
